description: Shared MySQL / MariaDB contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server. The MySQL collector (#488 / PR #88) shipped WITHOUT a fixture; issue #107 (Galera wsrep cluster state) adds this one and it becomes the source of truth, vendored byte-identical server-side. Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/mysql_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_mysql.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip with ONLY the CLI transport mocked -- each scenario's 'queries' bodies are fed back per statement (matched by longest query-needle so 'SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE ...' is not shadowed by the 'SHOW GLOBAL STATUS' probe prefix), and mysql_metrics(**config) must equal scenario['payload']. The server's spec/requests/api_collect_mysql_spec.rb posts scenario['payload'] under data['mysql'] through /collect and asserts Ingesters::Mysql ingests each shape (Galera present / absent / unreachable envelope). 'config' and 'queries' are agent-side inputs the server ignores. Change the payload shape only in lockstep across both repos, keeping the two copies byte-identical.
_agent_min_version_note: MINOR bump: Galera adds a new user-facing capability (cluster-state gauges + the server-side galera_cluster_degraded trigger). Released main is 1.13.1; the only PRs pushed above it are 1.14.0 (Docker image-inventory #102) and 1.14.1 (TSDB #103), so 1.15.0 is the next free minor. MySQL has NO server version gate (no FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS entry -- it is purely config-driven, mysql_enabled defaults false), so nothing gates on this number; it exists only to date the payload.
galera_contract: The Galera keys are the whitelisted subset of SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'wsrep%', merged into the SAME data['mysql'] object as the base metrics (no new payload key, no new config). Galera detection is IMPLICIT: a non-Galera server returns zero wsrep rows, so every wsrep_* key is simply ABSENT (no-data server-side, not null). The keys are likewise ABSENT when the reachability envelope reports unreachable/config_error -- the probe fails before the wsrep statement runs, so the payload is envelope-only. Never fabricate: a wsrep_* numeric that fails to parse (NULL / garbage), a non-finite float (inf/nan/overflow -- these would serialize as invalid Infinity/NaN JSON and poison the whole tick), and a present-but-blank status string are all OMITTED, not sent as null or empty. Every shipped float is therefore finite. All values are instantaneous gauges/status -- nothing to rate; ints/floats are parsed to native types, non-blank status strings ship verbatim. Same absent-vs-null discipline as the rest of the reachable/error envelope from #488.

field_contract._base: reachable/connections/queries/slow_queries/aborted_connects/uptime/innodb_buffer_pool_hit_ratio/innodb_buffer_pool_usage_pct/max_connections/version/is_replica/replication are the pre-#107 MySQL payload (PR #88); unchanged here and included so the round-trip pins the WHOLE data['mysql'] object, not just the Galera delta.
field_contract.wsrep_cluster_size: wsrep_cluster_size -- number of nodes in the component this node sees (int). A drop below the configured size is the split-brain / lost-quorum signal.
field_contract.wsrep_cluster_status: wsrep_cluster_status verbatim -- 'Primary' when the node is in the primary component; anything else ('non-Primary', 'Disconnected') means it cannot serve writes. Drives galera_cluster_degraded server-side.
field_contract.wsrep_local_state: wsrep_local_state -- numeric node FSM state (int; 4 == Synced). Pairs with wsrep_local_state_comment.
field_contract.wsrep_local_state_comment: wsrep_local_state_comment verbatim -- human label for wsrep_local_state ('Synced', 'Donor/Desynced', 'Joining', 'Initialized').
field_contract.wsrep_ready: wsrep_ready verbatim -- 'ON' when the node will accept queries, 'OFF' when it will reject them.
field_contract.wsrep_connected: wsrep_connected verbatim -- 'ON' when the node has network connectivity to the cluster.
field_contract.wsrep_flow_control_paused: wsrep_flow_control_paused -- fraction of time (0.0-1.0) replication was paused by flow control since the last status read (float). Sustained > 0 means a slow node is throttling the cluster.
field_contract.wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg: wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg -- average length of the local received-write-set queue (float). > 0 means this node is falling behind on apply.
field_contract._dropped: Every other wsrep_* row (wsrep_provider_name, wsrep_protocol_version, wsrep_local_state_uuid, ...) is NOT ingested and is dropped from the payload; only the eight keys above are whitelisted.

galera_healthy.description: A healthy 3-node Galera / MariaDB member: Primary component, local state 4/Synced, ready+connected ON, negligible flow control. Pins native typing (cluster_size/local_state ints, flow_control_paused/local_recv_queue_avg floats, status strings verbatim) and the whitelist drop of the extra wsrep rows (wsrep_protocol_version, wsrep_provider_name).

galera_degraded.description: A partitioned Galera node cut off from quorum: non-Primary component, cluster_size collapsed to 1, local state 0/Initialized, wsrep_ready OFF (rejects queries), heavy flow-control pausing and a backed-up recv queue. This is the shape that fires galera_cluster_degraded server-side. reachable stays true -- the node is up, the CLUSTER is degraded.

non_galera.description: A plain (non-Galera) MySQL 8 server. SHOW GLOBAL STATUS LIKE 'wsrep%' returns ZERO rows (empty stdout), so no wsrep_* key is emitted -- Galera detection is implicit (no-data == not clustered). The payload is exactly the pre-#107 base object; the server sees no Galera keys and treats the host as non-clustered.

unreachable.description: The reachability probe (SHOW GLOBAL STATUS) fails with a refused connection, so mysql_metrics returns the envelope only and never runs the wsrep statement. Proves the Galera keys are absent on unreachable -- the server must not read (or fabricate) cluster state from a host it could not reach.
